narrative.overview:
Skiptocyte looks like stain on paper, not like a dashboard. The canvas is a cool wash at hue 236, taken from the logo’s `#4A90B8`. Cards sit slightly lighter as paper. The only loud ink on a typical screen is the primary stain-blue CTA. IBM Plex Sans Variable carries every role — chrome, body, and the large tabular digits a tech reads at a glance.

Timers extend that wash into concurrent rings. A running card is primary-tinted paper with a hairline remainder arc. Pause shifts the whole card to slate-ochre. Done floods teal-green and breathes a halo. Status is the hue, not a badge rack. App chrome (nav, shadcn buttons, paper cards) stays on the 0.65rem radius scale; timer surfaces use fuller 1.35rem cards and fully round pills.

The world is a bench instrument: dense enough to keep eyes on the scope, quiet enough that color and digits do the talking. It refuses a second display face, hard offset shadows, and a single hero clock with leftover chips stacked underneath.
keyCharacteristics: Hue-236 stain-wash canvas, paper cards, primary CTA
IBM Plex Sans Variable only; tabular lining digits on clocks and counts
Soft paper lift; status on timers is wash hue plus a hairline arc
Pills on timer cards; rounded-md / 0.65rem on app chrome
Coffee gold reserved for the support CTA, not for status

rules.name: The Hue-236 Rule
rules.body: Identity lives on hue 236. Ochre, teal, coffee, and red are state, support, or alert — never a second brand.

rules.name: The Wash-Is-State Rule
rules.body: A timer’s status is the card’s wash (and matching ink, track, arc, chip). Do not add a second status language — dots, banners, or color-coded icons — on top of the wash.

rules.name: The Tabular Digit Rule
rules.body: Clocks, counters, and add-chips use `tabular-nums lining-nums`. Proportional figures are for prose, not for time.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Sans Variable is the only family. Do not introduce a display serif, a mono clock face, or a system UI font for chrome.

rules.name: The Equal-Ring Rule
rules.body: On Timers, every running wait is the same card in a wrapping grid. Do not promote one timer into a hero and demote the rest to chips or a list.

rules.name: The Paper-Lift Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a soft dual shadow in ink, never a hard offset or a black slab. The done pulse is a halo in teal, not a bounce or a drop.

rules.name: The Pill-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: Fully round pills live on timer wash cards. App chrome stays on the 0.65rem radius scale. Do not pill the nav, and do not square the timer actions.

rules.name: The Hairline Arc Rule
rules.body: Remaining time is a thin remainder stroke on a fainter track, not a pie fill, not a thick progress bar, not a linear bar across the card.

dos: Do keep identity on hue 236: canvas, paper, primary, running wash, running arc.
Do set timer status by recoloring wash, ink, track, arc, and chip together.
Do set remaining time with a hairline remainder arc (track 1.35, arc 2.1, round cap).
Do use IBM Plex tabular lining digits for clocks, counters, and time chips.
Do put timer actions in fully round pills on 1.35rem wash cards, and keep app chrome on the 0.65rem radius scale.
Do honor reduced motion: no done pulse, no arc dash animation.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface or a dedicated clock/mono face.
Don't paint a running timer ochre or teal; those hues are pause and done only.
Don't replace the remainder arc with a pie, a thick ring, or a linear bar.
Don't use coffee gold for status, alerts, or primary actions.
Don't stack leftover timers as a list under one hero clock.
